security_audit.summary: Most external command and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting and safety documentation. The real risks are authenticated local HTTP write capability, environment or config based credential handling, and destructive Logseq operations that need stronger safeguards.

remediation.issue: Configurable API endpoint can receive bearer tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Default to loopback only, warn or block non-loopback URLs, and require HTTPS for any remote endpoint.

remediation.issue: Delete methods can remove Logseq pages or blocks without enforced confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run and explicit confirmation parameters before delete_page, delete_block, and bulk destructive workflows.

remediation.issue: API token may be read from environment variables or plaintext local config.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or OS secret storage, avoid repo-local token files, and redact tokens from logs.

remediation.issue: Write operations have limited audit support in the main library.
remediation.suggestion: Log method names, targets, and timestamps for write operations while excluding content bodies and tokens.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable API URL Sends Bearer Token
semantic_findings.description: The writer reads LOGSEQ_API_URL or a local config URL and then sends an Authorization bearer token to that URL. Without a loopback allowlist or scheme check, a bad configuration can expose the token to an untrusted endpoint.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code combines configurable destination selection with token loading and an Authorization header. The default is local, so the risk depends on configuration rather than clear malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Logseq Write Methods Lack Confirmation Parameter
semantic_findings.description: The skill exposes delete operations for pages and blocks that call Logseq deletion APIs after existence checks. The library functions do not require a confirmation parameter, so unintended calls can remove graph data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented API includes delete_block, and the implementation calls deletePage and removeBlock directly. Safety guidance exists, but the callable methods themselves do not enforce confirmation.

content.value_statement: AI conversations and project notes often stay outside the user knowledge graph. This skill writes pages, blocks, tags, and properties to Logseq through its local HTTP API.
actual_capabilities: Creates Logseq pages with optional first block content and properties.
Adds child or sibling blocks under a page title or block UUID.
Updates block content and appends timestamped notes to pages.
Sets, removes, and batches block properties with basic type conversion.
Adds or removes tags by editing existing block content.
Loads API URL and token from environment variables or local config.
limitations: Requires the Logseq HTTP API to be enabled and reachable locally.
Requires a valid API token before any write operation can run.
Can modify or delete graph data, so users must confirm targets.
Does not include advanced conflict handling or graph backup features.

output_examples.output: Added the interview notes to Research/Interviews and applied the insight tag to the new block.

output_examples.input: Set the status property on this block to Complete and add the Review tag.
output_examples.output: Updated the block properties and added the Review tag without changing the existing text.

best_practices: Test writes in a disposable Logseq graph before using a production graph.
Prefer append operations when preserving existing notes matters.
Confirm UUIDs, page titles, and destructive actions before running writes.
anti_patterns: Do not store API tokens in shared repositories or exported graph files.
Do not run delete operations without checking the target and its children.
Do not send unreviewed bulk updates to a large graph.

faq.question: Does this skill require Logseq to be running?
faq.answer: Yes. Logseq must be running with the HTTP API enabled and reachable from the local machine.

faq.question: Where does the API token come from?
faq.answer: The script reads a provided token, LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN, or a local .claude logseq config file.

faq.question: Can it delete Logseq content?
faq.answer: Yes. The library includes page, block, property, and tag removal operations, so deletion needs explicit user review.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill workflows.

faq.question: Does it connect to external services?
faq.answer: It defaults to a local Logseq API endpoint, but the API URL can be changed by environment or config.

faq.question: Does it back up the graph before writing?
faq.answer: No. Users should back up important graphs before large updates or destructive operations.
